rounds.text: Gayatri Projects is currently trading at a significant valuation discount, evidenced by a P/E ratio of 6.39x compared to a sector benchmark of 13.81x [E1, E6]. This undervaluation is further underscored by an EV/EBITDA ratio of 0.39x, which sits far below the sector benchmark of 8.46x [E11]. The company has demonstrated a dramatic operational turnaround, evidenced by a 176% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a quarterly operating margin expansion to 13% in September 2026 from 1% in the year-ago quarter [E16, E25]. Financial health has improved through aggressive deleveraging, with borrowings falling to Rs 103 Cr from Rs 311 Cr in the prior year [E33]. Institutional confidence is rising, as evidenced by promoters increasing their stake to 23.56% and foreign institutions increasing their holdings to 17.95% since December 2023 [E35, E36]. Conceded: the company faces long-term sales growth challenges with a 5-year compounded growth rate of -26% [E14, E57], high debtor days of 208 [E61], and significant contingent liabilities of Rs 1,215 Cr [E59].

The bull’s reliance on low valuation multiples like a 6.39x P/E [E1] and 0.39x EV/EBITDA [E11] ignores the reality that these figures are likely distorted by non-core earnings, specifically the Rs 2,157 Cr of "other income" included in the company's profits [E60]. While the bull highlights a 176% sales growth [E16], this must be weighed against the long-term structural decline of -26% over five years [E14, E57] and a recent -9% contraction in compounded profit growth [E19]. Conceded: the company has reduced its debt to Rs 103 Cr [E33, E53]. However, this improvement is overshadowed by a cash conversion ratio of only 0.24x, suggesting that reported profits are not being matched by actual cash inflows [E28]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding institutional interest ignores the fact that domestic institutions have actually reduced their holdings [E37]. Finally, the company’s underlying operational instability is confirmed by the "inconsistent" trend in operating margins over the last two quarters [E27].
